name: Hodiah
overview: Hodiah is a male figure mentioned in the book of Nehemiah, identified as a non-Levite leader. His name appears on the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, specifically in verse 18. Although his tribal affiliation is not specified, his leadership role is notable within the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Hodiah means "grandeur is YHWH," reflecting a theophoric element that honors the greatness of God. This proper name, found in Nehemiah 10:18, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a significant meaning that acknowledges God's majesty.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hodiah is a descendant of Jacob, linking him to the broader Israelite lineage. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented for Hodiah in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hodiah's significance lies in his role as a leader who was not a Levite, highlighting the involvement of various Israelite groups in the covenant renewal community after the exile. His inclusion on the sealed document in Nehemiah demonstrates his commitment to the covenant and the restoration efforts led by Nehemiah. This underscores the collective responsibility of Israel's leaders in upholding God's law and reestablishing faithful worship.
